name: CA-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 25 points in the San Jose/Silicon Valley area
Liccardo has raised $3.5 million against a challenger who reported raising $400
No outside spending targets the incumbent and no polls show vulnerability
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: A D+25 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with essentially no campaign resources leave no plausible path to a Republican win; markets price the Democratic side near 96% and no polling or outside spending signals any vulnerability.
model.watch: Late outside spending against Liccardo or an unexpected scandal would be the only realistic route to narrowing this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
CA-16 covers much of San Jose and Silicon Valley and leans Democratic by about 25 points. First-term incumbent Sam Liccardo is seeking re-election against Republican Peter Soule, who has reported raising only $400. Liccardo has raised roughly $3.5 million and holds $2.2 million on hand, with no outside groups spending against him. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent.

The structural picture points firmly to Liccardo. The district's strong partisan lean, his incumbency, and his financial dominance leave the challenger without visible resources to compete. With no polling and no opposition spending, there is little evidence of vulnerability, and the race rates as Safe Democratic.
